title: Film review: Andhaa Kaanoon is what they call a masala film
author: S. Venkat Narayan
claims: Bachchan plays an honest forest officer jailed for 20 years for a murder he did not commit; his wife (Madhavi) is dishonoured by goondas, throttles their daughter and kills herself. After release he chases the forest contractor (Amrish Puri) into the courtroom and stabs him before the judge who convicted him. Bachchan 'appears content playing a secondary role'; the court scene is 'one of the most gripping and memorable on the Hindi screen'; he 'shows his flair for comedy in a song sequence in which he cajoles his wife in vain to plant a kiss on his cheek'. He reportedly charged Rs 1 lakh a day. The reviewer predicts a blockbuster.
notes: Magazine issue of 30 April 1983, republished online in 2013; text read from the page's JSON-LD articleBody.

title: Manmohan Desai and Prakash Mehra stand out as remarkable survivors with big budget films
author: Sumit Mitra
claims: Coolie was made at a cost of Rs 2 crore and netted Rs 3.5 crore from the sale of distribution rights before its 2 December 1983 release; it had passed Rs 1 crore in the Bombay territory and earned at least Rs 80 lakh in every major territory. Sharaabi was pre-sold at Rs 35 lakh per major territory. Describes the shooting of Mard, with Bachchan as the anti-imperialist champion of the underdog.

title: Release of Amitabh Bachchan film 'Shahenshah' delayed
author: M. Rahman
claims: Tinnu Anand signed Bachchan in 1983; his illness delayed shooting to late 1985. Meenakshi Sheshadri replaced Dimple Kapadia as heroine. The film was completed in October 1987 at an estimated cost of Rs 2.5 crore. Distribution rights were first sold at Rs 45 lakh per territory, then offered outright at a reported Rs 90 lakh per territory.
notes: Magazine issue of 31 January 1988, republished online in 2013.

title: Amitabh Bachchan makes spectacular come-back with Shahenshah
author: Simran Bhargava
claims: Released on 12 February 1988 amid threats from opposition youth wings, with record advance booking. The film is 'a rehash of everything Amitabh has ever done' and 'a long, somewhat irritating film with a familiar taste'. By day Bachchan plays a crude paan-chewing policeman, by night Shahenshah; Meenakshi Seshadri is 'the fresh, leggy heroine who lives in a slum'. The hero 'gets a beautiful woman's love'. In the finale he drives a truck into the courtroom and hangs the villain.
notes: Text read from the page's JSON-LD articleBody.

title: Amitabh Bachchan's future looks uncertain as 'Ganga Jamuna Saraswati' bombs
author: Salil Tripathi
claims: Released on 23 December 1988 in 270 theatres, the film 'had bombed' within a fortnight. Distributors paid up to Rs 75 lakh per territory. First-week Bombay collections were Rs 12.76 lakh (95 per cent of potential); in the second week revenue fell to 28–40 per cent. Critic Iqbal Masud called it 'trite and boring'; Bombay distributor Puran Chandra Rao said 'Amitabh has miserably disappointed'. Toofan's February release was postponed. Bachchan's new films included Jadugar, Toofan and Tinnu Anand's Satyam.
notes: Text read from the page's JSON-LD articleBody.

Bachchan, 'breathing fire and brimstone as the colonel and playing comedy as a Banaras ka bhaiya, partially recreates the old magic. But he looks haggard and weary to the bone.'

'As he locks eyes with Sridevi, the actress who plays his wife, Benazir, the screen is in danger of melting.' Badshah is beaten, tortured, imprisoned, shot at and bombed; for 18 years Benazir mumbles 'He will return'. Sridevi also plays the couple's daughter.

title: The preview, slide show and real video file of Major Saab

title: The Bade Miyan Chote Miyan review
claims: Arjun Singh (Bachchan) and Pyare Mohan (Govinda) are police friends; Arjun's sister Seema loves Pyare; Arjun 'has no female companion and some pretty crude comments are often passed about his age'. Neha (Ramya Krishnan) is a second eyewitness. Madhuri Dixit appears as herself. 'The film that's supposed to establish Amitabh's supremacy fails miserably'; as with Shakti, one star overshadows the other, 'here, it was just Govinda doing the overshadowing'.

'Bachchan is a natural with comedy, he can sleepwalk through the ma-beta bits, he can look convincing as a saviour.'

publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)

notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed.

title: Sooryavansham (1999)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)
claims: Thakur Bhanupratap Singh (Bachchan) is enraged when his son Heera (Bachchan) proposes to marry his childhood sweetheart Gauri, and more so when Heera backs down, promising never to marry; unknown to the father, Gauri refused an illiterate husband. Radha (Soundarya) loves Heera for his gentle manner and proposes; they leave the village, and he becomes a successful businessman and she a government officer.
notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed. Wikipedia instead says Bhanupratap arranged the Heera–Gauri marriage.

title: Hindustan Ki Kasam (1999)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)
claims: ABCL was first to produce the film. Bachchan's Kabeera was written loosely as a sutradhar (narrator), 'a man of no particular religion who speaks his mind'.
notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed.

title: Kohram (1999)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)
claims: Produced by ABCL. Jaya Prada plays Colonel Sodhi's wife Namrata; Tabu is a police officer in love with Major Ajit Arya. Mehul Kumar's project was first titled 'Aye Watan Tere Liye' with Bachchan, Dimple Kapadia, Arshad Warsi and Karisma Kapoor; Bachchan kept his commitment despite Mrityudaata's failure.
notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed.

title: Aks (2001)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)
claims: Produced by Bachchan and distributed by ABCL. At 58 Bachchan jumped 30 feet with Manoj Bajpayee for the waterfall scene. Nandita Das said at a press conference that her finished role was the opposite of what had been explained to her.
notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed.

title: Aankhen (2002)
publisher: Amitabh Bachchan - The Real Millenium Super Star (blog)
claims: The film had two endings: in the Indian one Bachchan's character repents and is locked away; in the overseas one he bribes the police. Bachchan returned to negative roles with this film.
notes: Read from the blog's Blogger feed.

title: Boom review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Saleem (Gulshan Grover) answers to Bade Mia (Bachchan), 'the kingpin, the father-figure and the most notorious gangster on India's Most Wanted list', and 'Bade Mia wants the diamonds back, come what may!' The action shifts to Bachchan, Grover and Zeenat Aman in Dubai. The critic wonders what Bachchan saw in 'an insipid role'; 'the veteran has a substantial role', but the director 'has wasted' him.
notes: Rating 1/5 from the page title.

title: Kerchief caper!
author: Seema Pant
claims: What sets Baghban apart is 'the on-going romance between the lead couple': Raj (Bachchan) and Puja (Hema Malini) 'are very much in love even after 40 years of marriage' and 'romance, sing and dance'. Raj gives his sons the last of his savings. When each son agrees to keep one parent for six months, Raj warns Puja, 'They want to separate us, not share our love', but defers to her; neither is happy apart, and the children ill-treat them. Alok loves them unconditionally, and the Patels become important in Raj's life. 'The film belongs to Amitabh Bachchan and Hema Malini. He sings, dances, romances, cries and makes you cry.'
notes: Rediff spells Hema Malini's character Puja; Wikipedia has Pooja.

title: Baghban review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: At his farewell party Raj Malhotra (Bachchan) announces that he wants to spend the rest of his life with his wife. Memorable scenes include Lilette Dubey reading Hema's letter to Amitabh after he breaks his glasses, and the climax, where 'Amitabh's oration' on the parent-child relationship 'is brilliant'. 'Amitabh Bachchan delivers a wonderful performance. Hema Malini looks elegant and conveys the pathos convincingly.'
notes: Wikipedia reports a two-star rating.

title: Khakee is money's worth. What more do you want?
author: Sukanya Verma
claims: 'At the fag end of his career, DCP Anant Shrivastava (Amitabh Bachchan) is finally asked to go on a life-threatening mission', having waited 'for an opportunity to prove his guts'; it comes as he and his wife (Jaya Prada) prepare for their daughter's wedding. 'Through DCP Anant Shrivastava, Santoshi expresses his anger at corruption, admonishes the media and the easily influenced masses.' Bachchan 'portrays his Anant Shrivastava with determination and grace'.

title: Khakee review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: The assignment is given to DCP Anant (Bachchan). Highlights: his pre-interval argument with Akshay Kumar, his argument with the villain, 'Amitabh's outburst at the police station, when he reminds the Officer Incharge of the duties of men in uniform', and the finale in which 'Amitabh and the villain come to blows'. 'In KHAKEE, Amitabh Bachchan delivers one of the best performances of his career.'
notes: Rating 4/5 from the page title.

title: So what's the deal about Aetbaar?
author: Gaurav Sharma
claims: A remake of Fear. The plot 'revolves around a small family of three with Amitabh (Dr Ranvir) as the head and Bipasha (Ria) as the daughter'; 'the rest of the plot is for the father to convince his daughter about Aryan's reality and to get even with him'. Bachchan sings a track. 'Slow and not at all gripping, not even when the father decides to go after Aryan.'

title: Aetbaar review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Aetbaar is about 'an over-possessive father out to save his daughter from the clutches of her weird lover'. Malhotra (Bachchan) 'believes he's simply a protective parent, while his daughter Ria believes he's simply possessive'; Aryan is 'the epitome of all the values that Ria's father abhors'.
notes: Rating 3/5 from the page title.

title: Dev: what's the fuss all about?
author: Vivek Fernandes
claims: Joint Police Commissioner Dev Pratap Singh (Bachchan) 'believes in serving and protecting the interests of the nation above all else' and is 'pigeonholed as a Muslim-hater'; his only son, aged 5, was killed by a bullet, and attempts have been made on his life and that of his wife, Dr Bharati (Rati Agnihotri). His friend of over 30 years, Special Commissioner Tejinder Khosla (Om Puri), turns bad; 'the scenes involving Bachchan and Puri make for the most riveting parts'. Farhan, who has tried to kill Dev, finally turns to him.

title: India Today's Kaveree Bamzai reviews film Dev by Govind Nihalani
author: Kaveree Bamzai
claims: 'One of the best things to have happened to post millennial Bollywood is the ageing of Amitabh Bachchan.' Dev is possibly 'the most brutal look at communal riots in mainstream cinema so far'. 'Bachchan is like the Glenfiddich he and Om Puri drink: impeccable and elegant.'
notes: Text from the page's JSON-LD articleBody.

title: Dev review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'DEV is about Dev [Amitabh Bachchan] and Tej's [Om Puri] friendship', 'a bond stronger than blood ties'; their conversations 'veer into a sermonizing mood'. 'It would be difficult to imagine anyone except Amitabh Bachchan enacting the title role.' 'Rati Agnihotri is competent.'
notes: Rating 2/5 from the page title.

title: Lakshya review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'Amitabh Bachchan doesn't get much scope, but his work is commendable. His dialogue in Marathi will meet with a thunderous response in Maharashtra.'
notes: Rating 2.5/5 from the page title.

title: Deewaar: Let's Bring Our Heroes Home
author: Derek Elley
claims: Major Kaul (Bachchan, 'in full Alec Guinness Kwai mode') has been 'rotting in a Pakistani POW camp for the past 33 years but still dreaming of returning to India'; the film opens with his 18th escape attempt. 'Kaul's wife, Nanda (Tanuja), never stopped believing he was alive, but his son, Gaurav, long ago lost hope.' The opening reels dwell on 'Kaul's physical humiliation by his leering Pakistani captors and his stiff-backed resistance'.
notes: Variety spells the character Ranbir.

title: Deewaar review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Gaurav decides to bring his father, Major Ranvir Kaul (Bachchan), back home, aided by Khan. 'It is Amitabh Bachchan who towers above all with a splendid and power-packed performance'; it is his third memorable performance of the year, after Khakee and Dev.
notes: Wikipedia reports a 3/5 rating.

title: Kyun! Ho Gaya Na review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Malhotra's dear friend Raj Chauhan (Bachchan) 'has dedicated his life to a small orphanage he runs at his home'. Amitabh enters at the intermission, when the story shifts to the orphanage children, whose pranks 'fall flat'. 'Even the climax, when Amitabh reveals his game-plan, does not have the desired impact. Amitabh Bachchan is extremely likeable.'

title: Why is Amitabh in Hum Kaun Hai?
author: Malishka Mendonsa
claims: The posters showed Bachchan as the leading man, but 'Amitabh, in fact, has an extended guest appearance. He is like a poster boy, trying to attract the audiences.' Dimple Kapadia plays an overprotective mother of two photosensitive children.

title: Hum Kaun Hai review
author: Manish Gajjar
claims: Sandra's husband, Major Frank John Williams (Bachchan), is at war with no news of his return; on her way through the woods Sandra bumps into Frank, who, with his friend Virendra (Dharmendra), 'begins to investigate the mystery surrounding his family'. 'Amitabh Bachchan makes a special appearance in the film even though the publicity showed him as the central character.'
notes: Published September 2004 per the URL path; the page gives no exact date.

title: Ab Tumhare Hawale is a muddle!
author: Patcy N
claims: After Vikramjit (Bobby Deol) dies for the nation, his son Kunal is 'forced to join the army by his grandfather (Amitabh Bachchan)'. 'Amitabh talks about his son Bobby proving himself in the war', then ends 'mouthing clichés about always wanting peace'. 'Amitabh Bachchan is seen far too often in these officer roles and has nothing at all new to offer in this uniformed outing.'

title: Ab Tumhare Hawale Watan Sathiyo review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: The film 'tells the story of Amarjeet Singh [Amitabh Bachchan], an army officer, who watches his son Vikramjeet Singh [Bobby Deol] sacrifice his life for the nation'. 'Amitabh Bachchan breathes fire when he confronts his opponents.'

title: With 'Black', Sanjay Leela Bhansali attempts a monochromatic leap forward for Indian cinema
claims: Bachchan calls Black 'the most exhausting film he has ever made'. 'The movie belongs to Bachchan and Rani Mukherji, both of whom spent six months learning sign language for the blind.' Bhansali 'marvels at the way Bachchan uses the power of silence'.
notes: Text from the page's JSON-LD articleBody; no byline in the extract.

title: Black: Bhansali's passion, pain and pleasure
author: Sita Menon
claims: Debraj Sahai (Bachchan) 'wrangles himself into the responsibility of turning the blind, deaf and mute girl into a fine young lady'; Michelle's father fumes at 'the drunk, ill-mannered teacher'. The review notes comic touches, such as Bachchan swearing in sign language, and the late scene in which 'Debraj stretches Michelle's hand out the window and into the rain'.
notes: URL not cited in the Wikipedia article; found by Rediff's date pattern.

title: Waqt loses the race
author: Vishal D'Souza
claims: Ishwarchand Thakur (Bachchan) is a 'postman-turned-toy maker and industrialist' who 'dotes devotedly on Adi who can do no wrong, much to the dismay of his wife (Shefali Shah)'. He sends Aditya packing because he 'hides a deep painful secret that he cannot yet share with Aditya'. The repartee of Bachchan, Boman Irani and Rajpal Yadav ensures 'laughs aplenty'.
notes: URL not cited in the Wikipedia article; found by Rediff's date pattern.

title: Bunty Aur Babli (2005) review
author: Jaspreet Pandohar
claims: The film teams Bachchan with his son Abhishek. 'Bachchan Sr plays Police Commissioner Dashrath Singh, a sarcastic cop hot on the trail of elusive con artists Bunty (Abhishek Bachchan) and Babli (Rani Mukerji).'

title: Paheli is a breathtaking dream
author: Raja Sen
claims: On the way to the king, the villagers are 'stopped by an eccentric old shepherd, who solves the day with superb, obvious efficiency'. 'Amitabh Bachchan, kajal-eyed and wonderfully mad, is startlingly fantastic in this cameo.'

title: Sarkar is just Godfather, dumbed-down
author: Raja Sen
claims: 'Amitabh Bachchan is Sarkar, the Goodfather', 'a mafiosi leader with a strong NGO streak' who 'sits and listens to unjust tales, sending out a righteous army of goons'; his resemblance to Bal Thackeray is 'entirely superficial'. 'Amitabh is incredibly restrained, his character bereft of soliloquy and bluster', and 'given surprisingly little room to perform'. 'Supriya Pathak is perfect as Amitabh's submissive wife.' The film is 'Coppola by numbers'.

title: Sarkar review
author: William Thomas
claims: A 'violent family saga, loosely inspired by The Godfather'. 'Aging Sarkar (or Don) Subhash Nagare (Amitabh Bachchan in a powerhouse performance) is head of the Nagare family working outside the system due to exclusion by social prejudice.'
notes: The page's datePublished is a placeholder (2000-01-01), so no date is entered.

title: AB shines, Viruddh doesn't
author: Savera Someshwar
claims: Bachchan is 'both the star and the soul' of the film. The first half draws the viewer into 'the comfortably warm world of Vidyadhar (Amitabh) and Sumitra Patwardhan (charmingly played by Sharmila Tagore)': 'Their banter, their daily routine underline a bond built over the years. They really look like a couple who, having faced the vicissitudes of life, are now in complete harmony with each other.' They welcome their son's British girlfriend at once; Amar's death is 'a huge blow to his parents', and the second half turns melodramatic.

title: Viruddh review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Viruddh is 'about an aged couple fighting tooth and nail to prove that their slain kid was not a drug peddler', and it 'follows a similar path' to Baghban 'as far as the compatibility of the couple is concerned'. 'The sequences between Amitabh and Sharmila are interesting and so identifiable, you don't really mind the slow pacing of the narrative.'
notes: Rating 3/5 from the page title.

title: Just another love story
author: Sukanya Verma
claims: 'Amitabh Bachchan as Jai's pampering Pa and Revathy as his traditionalist Mom complete the family portrait.' In the song 'Mere Munna', 'Big B is liveliness personified'. 'His portrayal of an affectionate father is lined with warmth and spirit.'

title: Amrithdhare: A must watch!
author: Lata Jha
claims: 'Three days of meaningful living is worth many lifetimes of meaningless existence' is 'the message put forward by Amitabh Bachchan in his flash appearance towards the end' of this Kannada marital drama about Puru and Amritha.

title: Amitabh rocks in Ek Ajnabee
author: Vipin Vijayan
claims: Based on Man on Fire, the film 'reinvents Vijay Dinanath Chauhan'. Bachchan plays retired Indian Army Colonel Suryaveer Singh, called to Bangkok by Shekhar to guard eight-year-old Anamika, only daughter of a millionaire couple. During an engagement with terrorists in Kashmir he accidentally shot dead two children, one reason for his heavy drinking. Anamika 'breathes in life into the dead soul of Suryaveer'; after she is kidnapped he 'swears to bring the culprits to book'.

title: Ek Ajnabee review
author: Manish Gajjar
claims: Suryaveer was chosen because Anamika's mother wanted a bodyguard who would also be a friend to her daughter. The girl brings out 'the emotions which have been suppressed by Suryaveer all these years'; when all plans for her release fail, he takes matters into his own hands.
notes: Published December 2005 per the URL path; the page gives no exact date.

title: Don't visit this Family
author: Raja Sen
claims: Bachchan plays Sushant Singh's father, 'a nefarious Dubai-based baddie'. When a misguided bullet hits do-gooder Shekhar (Akshay Kumar), Bachchan kills him to leave no witnesses and drives away. 'Amitabh inexplicably keeps licking his chops'; the stars 'just went through the motions after pocketing fat paychecks'.
notes: Rediff names the character Biren Sahi and places him in Dubai; Wikipedia and India Today say Bangkok.

title: Movie review: 'Family: Ties of Blood' starring Amitabh Bachchan, Akshay Kumar
claims: 'Bachchan, as a mafia don who lives in Bangkok, smokes a cigar, wears nifty pinstripes, and looks irritated to be playing the bad guy in a poorly written role.' 'Bachchan's Missing-in-Action performance does nothing either for his oeuvre or for his admirers.'
notes: Text from the page's JSON-LD articleBody; no byline in the extract.

title: Darna Zaroori Hai review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Story 2 (Bachchan and Ritesh Deshmukh, directed by Ram Gopal Varma): 'An aged professor [Bachchan] believes there's someone in his house'; his student advises him to seek psychiatric help, and 'the invisible man finally appears in the mirror'. 'Technically, this isn't a scary story; it has more of shock-value.'
notes: Rating 1.5/5 from the page title.

title: Kabhi Alvida Naa Kehna review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'Amitabh Bachchan's philandering lifestyle provides ample moments of laughter and of course, eye-candy, what with some gorgeous firang babes jumping out of the closet.' He hosts a dinner on Kirron Kher's birthday. The relationship 'between the parent and child [the Bachchans] is delicately handled'. 'Amitabh Bachchan is in superb form.'

title: Review: KANK is an exhausting film
author: Raja Sen
claims: Bachchan plays Abhishek's 'flamboyant dad Sam (sexy Sam, the background score keeps reminding us)', 'a widower who dresses like Snoop Doggy Dogg and cavorts appropriately with blondes'; 'it's fabulous to see Bachchan relish this campy role'. The most compelling character in the film is 'a dad who dresses rather bizarrely'.
notes: URL not cited in the Wikipedia article; found by Rediff's date pattern. Wikipedia quotes Raja Sen's criticism of the script.

title: Akshay Kumar gets a Bhojpuri makeover. Amitabh Bachchan & Dharmendra did it first
author: Harsh Tiwari
claims: Bachchan appeared in the Bhojpuri film Ganga (2006) and its sequel Gangotri (2007). Ganga 'revolves around a young woman in love with Shankar'; 'Thakur Vijay Singh, portrayed by Amitabh Bachchan, uses his influence in the village to arrange her marriage with his son Ranjit, setting the stage for a conflict rooted in power, class, and rural politics'. Hema Malini and Nagma 'also played pivotal roles'. The film was produced by Bachchan's make-up artist Deepak Sawant.
notes: Found by web search; a retrospective feature, not a contemporary review.

author: Sudarshana Dwivedi; Sukanya Verma

title: Eklavya is undeniably impressive
author: Raja Sen
claims: Bachchan narrates the opening credits, explaining the Mahabharata legend of Eklavya. The dying queen (Sharmila Tagore) is tended by the king, who recites Shakespeare's 18th sonnet to her. 'This is an out-and-out Amitabh Bachchan film. Eklavya is conflicted and determined, forceful yet fragile, and — using his eyes to masterful effect — Amitabh hands in a stunning performance.' Jimmy Shergill is 'pitted against Amitabh in the film's finest scene'.

title: Eklavya – The Royal Guard review

title: Nishabd is a powerful film
author: Raja Sen
claims: Varma extracts 'a phenomenal performance from The Megastar'. Standing on a precipice, Bachchan narrates 'the story of a girl that drove him to thoughts of suicide'. The first half focuses on 'the inevitable spark, the undeniable chemistry, between this perfectly cast odd-couple'; the performance is 'a reinvention so masterful that you can't help but marvel'.

title: Amitabh rocks Cheeni Kum
author: Raja Sen
claims: 'A deftly made May-December love story.' Buddhadeb Gupta (Bachchan), a London restaurateur and 'preachy perfectionist', lays sarcasm on Nina Verma (Tabu) when she sends back a dish, and is then compelled to apologise; 'He's 64, she's 34'. Nina 'lends the pair contrast, gives it chemistry, makes the film work'; 'the repartee between the lead pair is tight'.

title: Shootout at Lokhandwala review

title: Ram Gopal Varma ki.. Aargh!

Babban is 'so over-written it hurts'; 'Amitabh conjures up some great moments, but he was a better villain in Aks'.

title: Review: The Last Lear
author: Sukanya Verma

Shefali Shah plays 'his live-in companion'. 'This is Bachchan's masterpiece.'

title: 102 Not Out review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: '102 NOT OUT is an unusual story of a father and a son. Dattatraya Vakharia (Amitabh Bachchan) is a healthy old man at the ripe age of 102. title: Gulabo Sitabo review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'Amitabh Bachchan and Ayushmann Khurrana starrer GULABO SITABO is a decent entertainer despite the lack of humour and an average script.' Establishes the relationship: 'Mirza Chunnan Nawab (Amitabh Bachchan), 78, is married to Fatima Begum (Farrukh Jafar), who is nearly 17 years older to him'; Begum owns the century-old Fatima Mahal in Lucknow and, being old 'and also a bit delusional', leaves Mirza to take care of the haveli. Baankey Rastogi's family have been tenants 'since ages' paying merely ₹30 monthly rent, which Mirza wants raised so he can drive them out. Notes the film premiered on a digital platform.
notes: Supports the age gap, the marriage's property basis and the Mirza-Baankey feud used in PAIR-095. No publication date on the page.

title: Chehre review
author: Taran Adarsh

Lateef stakes his legal reputation on proving Sameer's part in Oswal's murder. 'Amitabh Bachchan's entry is clap worthy.' Recalls his 'No Means No' dialogue in Pink (2016).
notes: No publication date on the page.

title: Jhund review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: Rated 4/5. 'JHUND is the story of an unusual football team. Vijay Borade (Amitabh Bachchan) teaches in St John's college', which stands next to a vast slum. He spots slum youths playing football with an abandoned plastic box, goes to the slum the next day and asks them to play for thirty minutes; the children become so attached to the game that 'they agree to play without money'. Vijay proposes a friendly match against the college team, whose coach 'despises these slum children' and pressures his side to score ten goals without conceding.
notes: No publication date on the page.

title: Goodbye review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'Despite the performances GOODBYE suffers from a weak second half and depressive tone.' Tara learns of her mother Gayatri's death when 'her father Harish (Amitabh Bachchan) calls'; she and Harish 'don't see eye to eye and both clash over the funeral ceremonies', and Harish is upset that Karan and Angad 'don't seem moved by their mother's demise', his behaviour leading to fights in the house. Praises the scene in which the family imagine Gayatri talking to them and 'the animation flashback of Amitabh Bachchan and Neena Gupta', but notes that this and Gayatri's love for the ukulele 'never gets established in the flashback portions'.
notes: The last observation is the basis for creating no Romances row for Harish and Gayatri. No publication date on the page.

title: Uunchai review
author: Taran Adarsh
claims: 'UUNCHAI is a simple, emotional, family film with top notch performances by the lead cast.' 'Amit Shrivastava (Amitabh Bachchan) is a successful author, based in Delhi. He is separated from his wife Abhilasha (Nafisa Ali Sodhi) and the closest people in his life are his three friends – Javed (Boman Irani), Om Sharma (Anupam Kher), and Bhupen (Danny Denzongpa).' Bhupen proposes the Everest Base Camp trek and the others refuse on grounds of age and health; after his death Amit finds that Bhupen had booked the tour for his three friends. Notes this is the director's first film celebrating friendship rather than family.
notes: The source for Amit's separation from Abhilasha, which is stated but not developed in the film. No publication date on the page.
